SQLite3 Multiple Ciphers — vendored amalgamation provenance (Step 90, ADR-0021; release moved by Step 165)

sqlite-version: 3.54.1

embedded-licenses: BSD-3-Clause (SHA-2); MIT (AEGIS, miniz); Unlicense (a part of miniz); CC0-1.0 (fastpbkdf2, Base64); CC0-1.0 OR Apache-2.0 (Argon2); ISC (libsodium); public domain (MD5, SHA-1, Rijndael, ChaCha20 and Poly1305, Ascon)

Verification performed at vendoring (2026-11-23):
- asset-sha256 recomputed locally (`sha256sum`) equals the asset's line in the
  release's `sqlite3mc-2.7.1-SHA256SUMS`.
- The SHA256SUMS signature (`sqlite3mc-2.7.1-SHA256SUMS.sig`, Sigstore keyless:
  base64-encoded DER ECDSA) verifies with `openssl dgst -sha256 -verify` against the
  public key of the accompanying certificate (`sqlite3mc-2.7.1-SHA256SUMS.pem`,
  base64-encoded PEM): "Verified OK". Certificate: issuer O=sigstore.dev,
  CN=sigstore-intermediate; serial 74B05ED601CAB26012800102F1C4DA8DF88731D7;
  validity 2026-11-15T10:57:16Z – 11:07:16Z; SAN URI
  https://github.com/utelle/SQLite3MultipleCiphers/.github/workflows/build-reusable.yml@refs/heads/main;
  SHA-256 fingerprint 7A:9C:D4:00:37:05:74:66:DB:B7:9F:B9:5B:7D:AE:96:67:45:5E:38:0B:1F:74:E0:38:6E:B9:A7:21:C2:71:E2.
- NOT verified locally (no cosign on the vendoring machine): the certificate chain to
  the Fulcio root and the Rekor transparency-log inclusion. `cosign verify-blob` on a
  machine that has it closes that gap.
- Both files are vendored byte-for-byte from the zip. Not vendored (not build inputs):
  shell3mc_amalgamation.c, sqlite3.h, sqlite3ext.h, README.md.
- The embedded license headers were read file by file. Since 2.6.0 the
  hardware-accelerated ChaCha20 and Poly1305 paths are libsodium's source
  (ISC, Copyright (c) 2013-2026 Frank Denis): the amalgamation carries none of
  libsodium's notice (only D. J. Bernstein's "Public domain" on chacha-merged.c), so
  THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES and about.hbs carry it. 2.6.0 and 2.6.1 were skipped: their
  hardware-accelerated ChaCha20 carried a block-counter overflow into the nonce where
  the scalar code wraps it, so a page written past the wrap decrypted silently wrong
  on the other code path; 2.7.0 prevents the overflow.

Re-vendoring (an SQLite3MC release bump): download the new amalgamation zip plus
SHA256SUMS / .sig / .pem, verify as above, replace the two files, read the amalgamation's
embedded license headers file by file (no tool sees them), update every line of this
record, `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES` and the block in `about.hbs`, then run `cargo test -p kupferdraht-core --test step_90_sqlite3mc_engine` — it
pins the header's version defines and the SHA-256 of both files against this record.
